paper_title: LaSQuE Improved Zero-Shot Classification from Explanations Through   Quantifier Modeling and Curriculum Learning
model_annotation: The bar chart illustrates the relationship between attention weights and explanation length, as measured in the context of the LaSQuE model for zero-shot classification. The horizontal axis, labeled "Exp. Length," displays discrete values ranging from 5 to 35 in increments of 5, representing the length of generated explanations. The vertical axis, labeled "Attention Weights," is scaled linearly from 0.20 to 0.45, indicating the magnitude of attention assigned to different explanation lengths. Each bar corresponds to a specific explanation length and is colored uniformly in blue. The attention weights peak at an explanation length of 15, with a value of approximately 0.41, and again at 20, with a value of about 0.40. The weights decrease at lengths 5 (≈0.38), 25 (≈0.36), 30 (≈0.32), and 35 (≈0.34). The bars are arranged in ascending order of explanation length from left to right, and no grouping or stacking is present. There is no visual emphasis (e.g., shading or annotation) on any particular bar, and the chart lacks a legend, implying a single metric is being displayed. The overall trend suggests that attention is most focused on explanations of intermediate length (15–20), with lower attention given to both shorter and longer explanations.
